Marta G: Hey — had an FSA claim denied today, reason 'not eligible / missing proof'. I uploaded a screenshot of my digital insurance card. Claim ID: 8-21456.
PeopleOpsBot: FYI your benefits submission was received and routed to benefits-team. Reference: ticket #B-987.
Sanjay Patel: Marta, which plan are you on (PPO/HMO) and do you have a member ID & group number on the card? Insurers often need group number.
Marta G: Core PPO (employer plan). My digital card shows Member ID 57-3342 but the group number field is blank on the portal. I thought the screenshot would be fine :/
Jordan (People Ops): Screenshots sometimes get rejected. Ask insurer for short form proof — a benefits verification letter or a PDF of the digital card. You can generate a downloadable ID card from the benefits portal: https://benefits.redwood.com -> My Coverage -> ID Card.
Jordan (People Ops): If you need the PDF filename it's usually `redwood-idcard-<lastname>-<memberid>.pdf`. Example:
```
redwood-idcard-gonzalez-573342.pdf
```
Jordan (People Ops): Also include an Explanation of Benefits (EOB) or an employer benefits verification email when you resubmit the FSA claim.
Alex L: If the portal doesn't show group number, try the insurer's member portal — sometimes group is on their PDF card. If still missing, benefits team can generate an official letter with group number.
Marta G: Thanks all. I called insurer and asked them to issue a benefits verification letter. Reopened claim with uploaded PDF and EOB. PeopleOpsBot updated ticket #B-987 -> status: waiting on insurer.
PeopleOpsBot: Reminder: FSA claims must include either insurer-issued ID card PDF or benefits verification letter plus itemized receipt. See internal doc: go/benefits-fsa-claims.
Marta G: Claim now accepted! insurer processed it and we have reimbursement pending. Appreciate the help :pray: 
Jordan (People Ops): Great — marking this thread resolved. If you want, we can add a short note to the benefits portal instructions to avoid screenshots.
